messages:
sasha: Hey team — running into weird timeouts on long streaming generations (>2m). I set client timeout to 300s but the request fails after ~60s with a ReadTimeout. Using python sdk 0.4.2. Anyone seen this?

mike: Hey @sasha — can you paste the exact client/config and the error log? Also mention any env vars like REDWOOD_* you might have set.

sasha: Sure, code is simple:
```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=..., timeout=300)
resp = client.chat.create(model='gpt-xyz', messages=msgs, stream=True)
for chunk in resp:
    print(chunk.text, end='')
```
Log: `requests.exceptions.ReadTimeout: HTTPSConnectionPool(host='api.redwood.com', port=443): Read timed out. (read timeout=60)`

mike: Two things that often bite here: (1) `timeout=300` is usually the total request/read timeout for non-stream calls, but streaming often enforces a per-chunk read timeout (default 60s) so long pauses between tokens still trigger. (2) underlying http client (requests/urllib3) semantics can be `(connect, read)` tuple. Try passing a tuple `timeout=(5,300)` or explicit stream-setting if the SDK exposes it. Also check env vars: `echo $REDWOOD_READ_TIMEOUT`

sasha: Tried `timeout=(5,300)` already, still got the `read timeout=60` in the trace. I don't have REDWOOD_READ_TIMEOUT set locally.

devx-ryan: FWIW we saw this exact symptom in an earlier SDK release — 0.4.2 accidentally left a hard-coded per-chunk timeout when streaming. The client arg got applied to non-stream reads but not to the streaming iterator. The stacktrace will show our internal `_stream_iter` where the timeout gets passed to `resp.iter_content(chunk_size=None, timeout=60)`.

eng-ml-lina: Confirmed. Root cause: bug in 0.4.2 where `stream` path used a fallback 60s chunk deadline and also an env var `REDWOOD_STREAM_CHUNK_TIMEOUT` (default 60) could override. Fix landed in 0.4.5 — it passes the read timeout through and supports setting chunk timeout to 0 to disable per-chunk enforcement for long generations.

sasha: Any safe workaround if we can't upgrade immediately?

mike: Two options: (A) set env var to disable chunk timeout: `export REDWOOD_STREAM_CHUNK_TIMEOUT=0` — this tells the SDK not to abort on long pauses between chunks; or (B) pin `requests`/`urllib3` and manually stream using lower-level client (ugh). Workaround (A) worked for a customer we assisted.

sasha: After `export REDWOOD_STREAM_CHUNK_TIMEOUT=0` it stayed alive past 2m. Nice. One more thing — we saw duplicated output when we enabled retries and a stream timed out mid-generation. Retries replayed the prompt and we ended up with doubled text. Is there a recommended retry policy for streaming endpoints?

devx-ryan: Yup — streaming endpoints are not idempotent when the server produced partial output. Recommended: disable automatic retries for streaming calls or only retry on connection-level failures before any token was emitted. In our client you can do: `client = RedwoodClient(..., retries={"max": 2, "on_stream": False})` or set `RETRY_ON_STREAM=false`. Also use an `idempotency_key` on requests if you need safe dedupe on server side.

mike: For reference, example config to reduce duplicate runs:
```python
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=..., timeout=(5,300), retries={"max":1, "on_stream": False})
resp = client.chat.create(..., stream=True, idempotency_key='job-123')
```
Note: idempotency only works if your server/workflow supports it — check the API docs.

sasha: Great — upgrading to 0.4.5 now and will test with `REDWOOD_STREAM_CHUNK_TIMEOUT=0` and retries disabled for streaming. Will post results. Thanks all :heart: :thumbsup:

support-bot: Follow-up: ticket #T-8421 created with logs attached and recommended patch applied to customer sandbox.
